The Aerosense measurement system uses low-cost, low-power MEMS sensors to measure local pressures, blade motions, and inflow conditions on wind turbine blades.
The system is composed of sensor nodes installed on the blades, a base station that collects and transmits the data, and a digital twin system for data processing and analysis.
The absolute pressure sensors have an absolute accuracy of ±50 Pa and a relative accuracy of ±2.5 Pa after calibration.
The differential pressure sensors have a pressure range of -2000 Pa to 2000 Pa with a precision of ±20 Pa.
The inertial measurement unit measures the blade motion and attitude at 100 Hz, which is used to correct the hydrostatic pressure variations.
Photogrammetry is used to determine the 3D shape and positions of the sensors on the blade, as the sensor node is manually installed.
The measurements on the 7 kW wind turbine showed that the pressure distribution can vary significantly during one rotation of the blade, even under stable wind conditions.
The Aerosense system uses a hybrid method to infer the local inflow conditions, including angle of attack and wind speed, without requiring a reference pressure measurement.

For a 5 MW wind turbine, the atmospheric pressure is about 50 times higher than the dynamic pressure, the hydrostatic pressure variation is about 40% of the dynamic pressure, and the pressure drift of the barometers is about 5% of the dynamic pressure.
The Aerosense system is designed to be easy to install, inexpensive, and non-intrusive, making it a cost-effective solution for the wind energy industry.
The digital twin system integrates the field measurements, automatically analyzes them, and enables comparison and improvement of low and high-fidelity simulations.
The Aerosense system can measure at up to 1.2 kHz, allowing the unsteady effects on the blade to be examined.
The researchers developed a dedicated sensor fusion algorithm to account for the large centrifugal accelerations experienced by the sensors on a wind turbine blade.

The influence of acceleration on the pressure measurements was experimentally quantified, showing a linear increase of 2.4 Pa/g when the sensor cavity is oriented in the direction of the acceleration.
The Aerosense system is designed to monitor the structural health of the blade in addition to the aerodynamic properties.
